paragraphs: Brixmor Property Group Inc. and subsidiaries (collectively, "BPG") is an internally-managed corporation that has elected to be taxed as a real estate investment trust ("REIT"). Brixmor Operating Partnership LP and subsidiaries (collectively, the "Operating Partnership") is the entity through which BPG conducts substantially all of its operations and owns substantially all of its assets. BPG owns 100% of the limited liability company interests of BPG Subsidiary LLC ("BPG Sub"), which, in turn, is the sole member of Brixmor OP GP LLC (the "General Partner"), the sole general partner of the Operating Partnership. Unless stated otherwise or the context otherwise requires, "we," "our," and "us" mean BPG and the Operating Partnership, collectively. We own and operate one of the largest publicly traded open-air retail portfolios by gross leasable area ("GLA") in the United States ("U.S."), comprised primarily of grocery-anchored community and neighborhood shopping centers. As of December 31, 2025, our portfolio was comprised of 348 shopping centers (the "Portfolio") totaling approximately 63 million square feet of GLA. Our high-quality national Portfolio is primarily located within established trade areas in the top 50 Core-Based Statistical Areas ("CBSAs") in the U.S., and our shopping centers are primarily anchored by non-discretionary and value-oriented retailers, as well as consumer-oriented service providers. As of December 31, 2025, our three largest tenants by annualized base rent ("ABR") were The TJX Companies, Inc., The Kroger Co., and Burlington Stores, Inc. In the opinion of our management, no material part of our business is dependent upon a single tenant, the loss of which would have a material adverse effect on us, and no single tenant or shopping center accounted for 5% or more of our consolidated revenues during 2025.

As of December 31, 2025, BPG beneficially owned, through its direct and indirect interest in BPG Sub and the General Partner, 100% of the outstanding partnership common units (the "OP Units") in the Operating Partnership. The number of OP Units in the Operating Partnership beneficially owned by BPG is equivalent to the number of outstanding shares of BPG's common stock, and the entitlement of all OP Units to quarterly distributions and payments in liquidation is substantially the same as those of BPG's common stockholders. BPG's common stock is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange ("NYSE") under the ticker symbol "BRX."

Management operates BPG and the Operating Partnership as one business. Because the Operating Partnership is managed by BPG, and BPG conducts substantially all of its operations through the Operating Partnership, BPG's executive officers are the Operating Partnership's executive officers, and although, as a partnership, the Operating Partnership does not have a board of directors, we refer to BPG's board of directors as the Operating Partnership's board of directors.

headings: Risks Related to Our Portfolio and Our Business
Adverse economic, market, and real estate conditions may adversely affect our financial condition, operating results, and cash flows.
Elevated levels of inflation and/or interest rates could adversely affect us and our tenants.
International trade disputes, including U.S. trade tariffs and retaliatory tariffs, could adversely impact our business.
We may be required to make rent or other concessions and/or incur significant capital expenditures to retain existing tenants or attract new tenants.
Our active value-enhancing reinvestment program subjects us to risks that could adversely affect our financial condition, operating results, and cash flows.
Significant retailer distress across our Portfolio could adversely affect our financial condition, operating results, and cash flows.
We may be unable to collect outstanding balances and/or future contractual rents due from tenants that file for bankruptcy protection.
Our expenses may remain constant or increase, even if income from our Portfolio decreases.
Our real estate investments are relatively illiquid, and we may not be able to dispose of assets in a timely manner, on favorable terms, or at all.
Our real estate assets may be subject to impairment charges.
We may be unable to obtain additional capital through the debt and equity markets on favorable terms or at all.
Our variable rate indebtedness subjects us to interest rate risk, and an increase in our debt service obligations may adversely affect our financial condition, operating results, and cash flows.
Adverse changes in our credit rating could affect our borrowing ability and the terms of existing or new financing.
Covenants in our debt agreements could, under certain circumstances, result in an acceleration of our indebtedness.
An uninsured property loss or a loss that exceeds the limits of our insurance policies could result in a loss of our investment or revenue associated with those properties.
Environmental conditions that exist at some of the properties in our Portfolio could result in significant unexpected costs.

The direct and indirect impact on us and our tenants from severe weather events, including flooding, wildfires, and hurricanes, could adversely affect our financial condition, operating results, and cash flows.
Public health crises could materially and adversely affect our financial condition, operating results, and cash flows.
We and our tenants face risks relating to cybersecurity incidents that could cause the loss of confidential information or other business disruptions.
Risks Related to Our Organization and Structure
BPG's board of directors may change significant corporate policies without stockholder approval.
BPG's board of directors may approve the issuance of stock, including preferred stock, with terms that may discourage a third party from acquiring us.
The rights of BPG and BPG's stockholders to take action against BPG's directors and officers are limited.
BPG's charter contains a provision that expressly permits BPG's non-employee directors to compete with us.
Risks Related to our REIT Status and Certain Other Tax Items
If BPG does not maintain its qualification as a REIT, it will be subject to tax as a regular corporation and could face a substantial tax liability.
Changes to the U.S. federal income tax laws, including the enactment of certain tax reform measures, could have a material and adverse effect on us.

Complying with REIT requirements may force BPG to liquidate or restructure investments or forgo otherwise attractive investment opportunities, and/or may discourage BPG from disposing of certain assets.
BPG may choose to make distributions in BPG's own stock, in which case stockholders may be required to pay income taxes without receiving any cash dividends.
paragraphs: Our Portfolio is predominantly comprised of community and neighborhood shopping centers. Our performance is, therefore, subject to risks associated with owning and operating these types of real estate assets. See "Forward-Looking Statements" included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K for the factors that could affect our rental income and/or property operating expenses and therefore adversely affect our financial condition, operating results, and cash flows.

Although recent inflationary pressures have begun to abate, certain price levels have remained high and inflation may increase in the future, and such increases could lead to the Federal Reserve increasing interest rates. Increases in interest rates could result in higher operating and incremental borrowing costs for us and our tenants. Although the terms of our leases, the duration of our indebtedness, and our relatively low exposure to floating rate debt have historically mitigated the direct impact of inflation and interest rate increases, the degree and pace of these changes have had and may continue to have impacts on our business, including as a result of increased financing costs when we refinance our indebtedness, and a potential economic recession, which may lead to higher levels of unemployment and decreases in consumer confidence and/or discretionary spending.

International trade disputes, including threatened or implemented tariffs imposed by the U.S. and threatened or implemented tariffs imposed by foreign countries in retaliation, could adversely impact our business. Many of our tenants sell imported goods and tariffs or other trade restrictions could increase costs for these tenants. To the extent our tenants are unable to pass these costs on to their customers, our tenants could be adversely impacted. In addition, international trade disputes, including those related to tariffs, could result in inflationary pressures that directly impact our costs, such as costs for steel, lumber, and other materials applicable to our redevelopment projects. Trade disputes could also adversely impact global supply chains which could further increase costs for us and our tenants or delay delivery of key inventories and supplies.

There are numerous shopping venues, including regional malls, outlet malls, other shopping centers, and e-commerce, which compete with our Portfolio in attracting and retaining retailers. As of December 31, 2025, leases are scheduled to expire in our Portfolio on a total of approximately 8.1% of leased GLA during 2026. We may not be able to renew or promptly re-lease expiring space and even if we do renew or re-lease such space, future rental rates may be lower than current rates and other terms may not be as favorable. In addition, we may be required to incur significant capital expenditures in order to retain existing tenants or attract new tenants. In these situations, our financial condition, operating results, and cash flows could be adversely impacted.

In order to enhance the attractiveness of our Portfolio to retailers and consumers, we actively reinvest in our assets in the form of repositioning and redevelopment projects. In addition to the risks associated with real estate investments in general, as described elsewhere, the risks associated with repositioning and redevelopment projects include: (1) delays or failures in obtaining necessary zoning, occupancy, land use, and other governmental permits; (2) abandonment of projects after expending resources to pursue such opportunities; (3) cost overruns; (4) construction delays; and (5) failure to achieve expected occupancy and/or rent levels within the projected time frame, if at all. If we fail to reinvest in our Portfolio or maintain its attractiveness to retailers and consumers, if our capital improvements are not successful, or if retailers and consumers perceive that shopping at other venues (including e-commerce) is more convenient, cost-effective, or otherwise more compelling, our financial condition, operating results, and cash flows could be adversely impacted.

Our income is substantially comprised of rental income from tenants in our Portfolio. Our income would be adversely affected if a significant number of our tenants failed to make rental payments when due as a result of either operating challenges or disruptions in credit markets that adversely affect the ability of our tenants to obtain financing on favorable terms or at all. If our tenants are unable to meet their rental obligations, renew leases, or enter into new leases with us, our financial condition, operating results, and cash flows could be adversely impacted.

Brixmor Operating Partnership LP and subsidiaries (collectively, the "Operating Partnership") is the entity through which BPG conducts substantially all of its operations and owns substantially all of its assets. BPG owns 100% of the limited liability company interests of BPG Subsidiary LLC ("BPG Sub"), which, in turn, is the sole member of Brixmor OP GP LLC (the "General Partner"), the sole general partner of the Operating Partnership. Unless stated otherwise or the context otherwise requires, "we," "our," and "us" mean BPG and the Operating Partnership, collectively. We own and operate one of the largest publicly traded open-air retail portfolios by gross leasable area ("GLA") in the United States ("U.S."), comprised primarily of grocery-anchored community and neighborhood shopping centers. As of December 31, 2025, our portfolio was comprised of 348 shopping centers (the "Portfolio") totaling approximately 63 million square feet of GLA. Our high-quality national Portfolio is primarily located within established trade areas in the top 50 Core-Based Statistical Areas in the U.S., and our shopping centers are primarily anchored by non-discretionary and value-oriented retailers, as well as consumer-oriented service providers. As of December 31, 2025, our three largest tenants by annualized base rent ("ABR") were The TJX Companies, Inc. ("TJX"), The Kroger Co. ("Kroger"), and Burlington Stores, Inc. ("Burlington"). BPG has been organized and operated in conformity with the requirements for qualification and taxation as a REIT under U.S. federal income tax laws commencing with our taxable year ended December 31, 2011, has maintained such requirements through our taxable year ended December 31, 2025, and intends to satisfy such requirements for subsequent taxable years.

Our primary objective is to maximize total returns to our stockholders through consistent, sustainable growth in cash flow. Our key strategies to achieve this objective include proactively managing our Portfolio to drive internal growth, pursuing value-enhancing reinvestment opportunities, and prudently executing on acquisition and disposition activity, while also maintaining a flexible capital structure positioned for growth. In addition, as we execute on our key strategies, we do so guided by our Corporate Responsibility strategy.
We believe the following set of competitive advantages positions us to successfully execute on our key strategies:

•Expansive Retailer Relationships – We believe that the scale of our asset base and our nationwide footprint represent competitive advantages in supporting the growth objectives of the nation's largest and most successful retailers. We believe that we are one of the largest landlords by GLA to TJX, Kroger, and Burlington, as well as a key landlord to most major grocers and retail category leaders. We believe that our strong relationships with leading retailers afford us unique insight into their strategies and priority access to their expansion plans.

•Fully-Integrated Operating Platform – We manage a fully-integrated operating platform, leveraging our national scope and demonstrating our commitment to operating with a strong regional and local presence. We provide our tenants with dedicated service through both our national accounts leasing team based in New York and our network of three regional offices in Atlanta, Philadelphia and San Diego, as well as our 10 leasing and property management satellite offices throughout the country. We believe that this structure enables us to obtain critical national market intelligence, while also benefiting from the regional and local expertise of our leasing and operations teams.

•Experienced Management – Senior members of our management team are seasoned real estate operators with extensive public company leadership experience. Our management team has deep industry knowledge and well-established relationships with retailers, brokers, and vendors through many years of operational and transactional experience, as well as significant capital markets capabilities and expertise in executing value-enhancing reinvestment opportunities.

截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，BPG 透過其對 BPG Sub 及 General Partner 之直接及間接權益，持有 Operating Partnership 之全部普通合夥單位（"OP Units"）。Operating Partnership 之 OP Units 數量與 BPG 之普通股數量相同，且所有 OP Units 之季度分紅及清算付款權利與 BPG 普通股股東 substantially the same。BPG 普通股於紐約證券交易所（"NYSE"）上市交易，股票代碼為 "BRX"。

paragraphs: Brixmor Property Group Inc. 以及其子公司（合稱為 "BPG"）為一間 internally-managed 公司，已選擇以不動產投資信託（"REIT"）方式課稅。Brixmor Operating Partnership LP 以及其子公司（合稱為 "Operating Partnership"）為 BPG 進行幾乎所有營運及擁有幾乎所有資產之實體。BPG 持有 BPG Subsidiary LLC（"BPG Sub"）100% 之有限責任公司權益，而 BPG Sub 則為 Brixmor OP GP LLC（"General Partner"）之唯一成員，該 General Partner 為 Operating Partnership 之唯一普通合夥人。除非另有說明或上下文另有要求，"we"、"our" 及 "us" 均指 BPG 及 Operating Partnership，合稱為。我們擁有並營運美國（"U.S."）以總可出租面積（"GLA"）計規模最大的上市開架式零售資產組合之一，主要由以超市為主力的社區及 neighbourhood 購物中心組成。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們的資產組合包含 348 個購物中心（"Portfolio"），總計約 63 平方英呎 GLA。我們高品質的全國性 Portfolio 主要位於美國前 50 名核心統計區（Core-Based Statistical Areas）中已建立之商業區，我們的購物中心主要由非奢侈性及價值導向之零售商，以及以消費者為導向之服務提供者為主力。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們年度租金（"ABR"）最大的三個租戶為 The TJX Companies, Inc.（"TJX"）、The Kroger Co.（"Kroger"）及 Burlington Stores, Inc.（"Burlington"）。BPG 自 2011 年財稅年度終結於 12 月 31 日起，已依照美國聯邦所得稅法規要求，組織並運作符合取得及課稅為 REIT 之條件，並持續維持此條件至 2025 年財稅年度終結於 12 月 31 日，並有意於後續財稅年度持續符合此條件。
我們的主要目標為透過持續且可持續之現金流成長，以最大化對股東之總回報。我們達成此目標之關鍵策略包括積極管理 Portfolio 以驅動內在成長、追求價值提升之再投資機會，以及謹慎執行買賣活動，同時也維持一具備成長彈性之資本結構。此外，我們在執行關鍵策略時，亦遵循我們的企業責任策略。
我們相信以下競爭優勢可使我們成功執行關鍵策略：
•廣泛的零售商關係 – 我們相信我們資產規模及全國性佈局，可為美國最大且最成功的零售商之成長目標提供競爭優勢。我們相信我們為 TJX、Kroger 及 Burlington 這三大零售商中，以 GLA 計最大的地主，同時也是大多數主要超市及零售類別領導者之關鍵地主。我們相信我們與領導零售商之間強大關係，使我們能獲得獨特的洞察他們策略，並有優先取得他們擴張計畫的機會。
•完整的運營平台 – 我們管理一完整的運營平台，運用我們的全國規模，並展現我們對強化區域及地方存在之承諾。我們透過位於紐約之全國租賃團隊及我們在亞特蘭大、費城及聖地牙哥之三個區域辦公室，以及我們全美各地 10 個租賃及物業管理衛星辦公室，為租戶提供專屬服務。我們相信此結構使我們能獲得關鍵的全國市場資訊，同時也能受益於我們租賃及運營團隊之區域及地方專業知識。
•經驗豐富的管理團隊 – 我們管理團隊之高階成員為經驗豐富的不動產經營者，具備廣泛的上市公司領導經驗。我們管理團隊具備深厚的產業知識，並透過多年之營運及交易經驗，與零售商、經紀人及供應商建立穩固關係，同時具備重要的資本市場能力及執行價值提升再投資機會之專業知識。

headings: 與本公司資產組合及業務相關之風險
不利的經濟、市場及不動產條件可能對本公司之財務狀況、營運成果及現金流產生負面影響。
高漲的通貨膨脹率及/或利率可能對本公司及其租戶產生負面影響。
國際貿易爭議，包括美國貿易關稅及報復性關稅，可能對本公司業務產生負面影響。
本公司可能需提供租金或其他讓步及/或進行重大資本支出，以維持現有租戶或吸引新租戶。
本公司積極的價值提升再投資計畫使本公司面臨可能對財務狀況、營運成果及現金流產生負面影響之風險。
本公司資產組閤中重大零售商財務困難可能對財務狀況、營運成果及現金流產生負面影響。
本公司可能無法收取租戶申請破產保護後所欠之應收帳款及/或未來契約租金。
本公司費用可能維持不變或增加，即使來自 Portfolio 的收入減少。
本公司不動產投資相對缺乏流動性，且可能無法及時以有利條件或任何方式處置資產。
本公司不動產資產可能面臨減值費用。
本公司可能無法以有利條件或任何方式透過債券及股權市場取得額外資金。
本公司浮動利率債務使本公司面臨利率風險，且本公司債務償還義務增加可能對本公司財務狀況、營運成果及現金流產生不利影響。
本公司信用評級惡化可能影響本公司借款能力及現有或新融資的條件。
本公司債務協議中的約束條款，於特定情況下，可能導致本公司債務加速償還。
未投保的財產損失或損失金額超過本公司保險政策的範圍，可能導致本公司投資或與這些財產相關的收入喪失。
本公司資產組閤中部分不動產所處的環境條件，可能導致重大且未預期的成本。
嚴重天氣事件，包括淹水、野火及颶風等，對本公司及其租戶所造成的直接與間接影響，可能不利於本公司財務狀況、營運成果及現金流。
公共衛生危機可能對本公司財務狀況、營運成果及現金流造成重大且不利的影響。
本公司及其租戶面臨與網路安全事件相關的風險，可能導致機密資訊遺失或其他營運中斷。
與本公司組織及結構相關的風險
BPG 的董事會可能在未經股東批准的情況下，改變重大企業政策。
BPG 的董事會可能批准發行股票，包括優先股，其條款可能阻卻第三方取得本公司。
本公司及本公司股東對 BPG 的董事及高階主管採取行動的權利受到限制。
BPG 的章程包含一項條款，明確允許 BPG 的非員工董事與本公司競爭。
與本公司 REIT 狀態及某些其他稅務項目相關的風險
若 BPG 未能維持其作為 REIT 的資格，將被視為一般公司課稅，並可能面臨重大稅務負擔。
美國聯邦所得稅法規的變更，包括某些稅制改革措施的實施，可能對本公司產生重大且不利的影響。
符合 REIT 要求可能迫使 BPG 進行資產處分或重整，或放棄其他具吸引力的投資機會，並可能使 BPG 放棄處分某些資產。
BPG 可能選擇以本公司股票作為分紅，此情況下股東可能需繳納所得稅，而未實際收到現金紅利。
paragraphs: 本公司資產組成主要為社區及 neighbourhood 購物中心。因此，本公司之表現受擁有及營運此類不動產資產之相關風險影響。請參閱本年度 10-K 報告中其他處所附之「前瞻性陳述」，以瞭解可能影響本公司租金收入及/或不動產營運費用之因素，進而對本公司財務狀況、營運結果及現金流產生不利影響。

儘管近期通貨膨脹壓力已開始減緩，但某些價格水準仍維持在高位，未來通貨膨脹可能進一步上升，此等上升可能導致聯邦儲備銀行提高利率。利率上升可能導致本公司及其租戶之營運成本及新增借款成本提高。儘管本公司租賃條款、債務期限及相對較低之浮動利率債務敞口歷來已緩解通貨膨脹及利率上升之直接影響，但這些變動之程度與速度已對本公司業務產生影響，包括因本公司重組債務時之融資成本增加，以及潛在經濟衰退，可能導致失業率上升及消費者信心及/或自願性支出減少。

國際貿易爭議，包括美國或外國為報復所威脅或實施之關稅，可能對本公司業務產生不利影響。許多租戶銷售進口商品，關稅或其他貿易限制可能增加這些租戶之成本。若本公司租戶無法將這些成本轉嫁給其客戶，則租戶可能受到不利影響。此外，國際貿易爭議，包括與關稅相關之爭議，可能導致通貨膨脹壓力，直接影響本公司成本，例如鋼鐵、木材及其他適用於本公司重建項目之材料成本。貿易爭議也可能對全球供應鏈產生不利影響，進而進一步增加本公司及其租戶之成本，或延遲關鍵存貨與物料之交付。

許多購物場所，包括區域性購物中心、折扣購物中心、其他購物中心及電商，與本公司資產競爭吸引及留住零售商。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司資產中租賃於 2026 年到期之租賃面積總計約為 8.1%。本公司可能無法續約或迅速重新出租到期空間，即使能續約或重新出租，未來租金率可能低於現行租金率，且其他條款可能不如現行有利。此外，本公司可能需投入大量資本支出以留住現有租戶或吸引新租戶。在這些情況下，本公司財務狀況、營運結果及現金流可能受到不利影響。

為提高本公司資產組對零售商及消費者之吸引力，本公司積極於資產上進行重新定位及重建項目之投資。除一般不動產投資之風險外，如其他處所述，重新定位及重建項目之風險包括：(1) 延誤或無法取得必要之 zoning、佔用、土地使用及其他政府許可；(2) 在投入資源追求機會後放棄項目；(3) 成本超支；(4) 建築工程延誤；(5) 未能在預期時間內達成預期之佔用率及/或租金水準，甚至完全無法達成。若本公司未能投資於資產組或維持其對零售商及消費者之吸引力，若本公司之資本改善未能成功，或若零售商及消費者認為其他場所（包括電商）更具便利性、成本效益或其它更具吸引力，則本公司財務狀況、營運結果及現金流可能受到不利影響。
本公司收入主要由資產組中租戶之租金收入組成。若大量租戶未能按期支付租金，因營運困難或信貸市場中斷而影響租戶取得有利條件之融資，則本公司收入將受到不利影響。若租戶無法履行租金義務、續約租賃或與本公司簽訂新租賃，則本公司財務狀況、營運結果及現金流可能受到不利影響。
